answers.reasoning: 1 is true: normal atmospheric pressure at sea level is about 101400 \(\mathrm{N/m^2}\). 2 is true: air presses equally in all directions at a place. 3 is false: when air moves faster its pressure decreases, not increases. 4 is false: air pressure falls with height and changes from place to place.

answers.value: Weight with kilogram is the incorrect pair
answers.reasoning: Weight is a force, so its SI unit is the newton (N), not the kilogram; the kilogram is the unit of mass. Density in \(\mathrm{kg/m^3}\), acceleration in \(\mathrm{m/s^2}\) and momentum in kg m/s are all correct pairs.

answers.value: Negative particles in the water are repelled and positive particles are attracted towards the comb
answers.reasoning: A comb rubbed in dry hair becomes negatively charged. It repels the negative charges in the water and pulls the positive charges to the near side, so the trickle bends towards the comb. A and C say the near side becomes negative, which is the opposite, so 'all above' cannot be right either.
Heat needed \(= m \times c \times \Delta T = 10 \times 0.11 \times 10 = 11\) cal.

1 is true: the laws of reflection are obeyed at every point even on a rough surface. 2 is true: the incident rays are parallel; they are scattered only because the surface is uneven. 3 is true: the normal points a different way at each point, so the angle of incidence differs from point to point. 4 is false: at any one point the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.

answers.value: Red giant, Sun, white dwarf, neutron star
answers.reasoning: A red giant is a star that has swollen hugely, so its density is the lowest. The Sun is an ordinary star. A white dwarf packs about a Sun's mass into the size of the Earth, and a neutron star packs it into a ball a few kilometres across, so it is the densest of all.

answers.runnerUp: D, if F means only the force of the water pressure on the base and the different water levels drawn in the figure are taken at face value
answers.reasoning: In A the object floats, in B it hangs in the water and in C it rests on the bottom. Whether the object floats, hangs or sinks, its whole weight is finally carried by the base, either through the water or by pressing on it directly. Each vessel has the same water and an object of the same mass, so the total force on each base is the same.

answers.value: I human, II bat, III rhinoceros
answers.reasoning: Region I lies only in the sonic circle: a human hears only sonic sound. Region II is sonic and ultrasonic: a bat hears both. Region III is sonic and infrasonic: a rhinoceros hears ordinary sound and also very low infrasonic sound. Option D puts the elephant in region I, but an elephant also hears infrasonic sound.
The coconut starts from rest, so \(h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times 1^2 = 4.9\) m.
The speed of sound in a medium is \(v = \sqrt{\frac{E}{\rho}}\), where E is the elasticity. For the same elasticity, the velocity is inversely proportional to the square root of the density.
1 unit = 1 kWh \(= 1000 \times 3600 = 3.6 \times 10^{6}\) J. So 10 units \(= 3.6 \times 10^{7}\) J. Option C, \(36 \times 10^{7}\), is ten times too large.

P is 3 cm from each mirror. Its image in the vertical mirror is 3 cm behind it, 6 cm from P; its image in the horizontal mirror is 6 cm from P in the other direction. P and the two images make a right triangle with legs 6 cm and 6 cm, so the area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 6 = 18\ \mathrm{cm^2}\).
Nickel and cobalt, like iron, are magnetic substances: a magnet attracts them. Magnesium and titanium are not attracted by a magnet, so they are non-magnetic.
At the centre of the Earth, g is zero because the Earth's mass pulls equally in all directions. Weight \(= mg = 60 \times 0 = 0\) N. The mass is still 60 kg.

answers.value: Q, R and S (land on horse, land on cart, horse on land)
answers.runnerUp: C, if the pull of the cart on the horse were counted as helping; but it acts backwards on the horse
answers.reasoning: The horse pushes the land backwards with its hooves (S), and the land pushes the horse forwards (Q); this forward push is what moves the horse and cart. The land also supports the cart on its wheels (R). The force of the cart on the horse (P) pulls the horse backwards, so it does not help.

1 is false: speed is distance per unit time, not the magnitude of displacement. 2 is true: in uniform motion the speed never changes, so average and instantaneous speed are equal. 3 is false: if the object turns back along the line, its distance and displacement differ, so average speed and average velocity differ. 4 is false: with uniform velocity the average velocity equals that velocity, not zero.

answers.reasoning: At a small height h, \(g_h = g\left(1 - \frac{2h}{R}\right)\), so a goes with 1. At depth h, \(g_d = g\left(1 - \frac{h}{R}\right)\), so b goes with 3. At the poles the Earth's radius is least, so g is maximum: c goes with 2.

answers.value: A horizontal line: total energy stays constant with height
answers.reasoning: As the object falls, potential energy turns into kinetic energy, but their sum stays the same (conservation of energy). So the graph of total energy against height is a horizontal straight line, which is graph D.

answers.value: X has the lower frequency and pitch; Y has the higher frequency and pitch
answers.reasoning: In the same time, wave X completes about one and a half oscillations while wave Y completes about three. So Y has the higher frequency. Pitch rises with frequency, so X has the lower pitch and Y the higher pitch.
Height climbed \(= 30 \times 0.20 = 6\) m. Work done \(= mgh = 50 \times 10 \times 6 = 3000\) J. Power \(= \frac{3000}{60} = 50\) W.

For the same metal, \(R \propto \frac{L}{A}\). From the figure: P is \(\frac{L}{A}\), Q is \(\frac{3L}{2A} = 1.5\frac{L}{A}\), R is \(\frac{L}{2A} = 0.5\frac{L}{A}\) and S is \(\frac{L}{A/2} = 2\frac{L}{A}\). In ascending order: R, P, Q, S.

answers.value: Sulphur dioxide, pure water, glass, nickel
answers.reasoning: Sound is slowest in gases, faster in liquids and fastest in solids. Sulphur dioxide (a gas) is slowest, about 220 m/s; pure water is about 1500 m/s; glass is a few thousand m/s; nickel, a metal, is about 6000 m/s and fastest.

answers.value: Concave mirror: image inverted and same size (h2 negative), u and v both negative and equal
answers.runnerUp: B, which is the same equations written another way (-h1 = h2 is h1 = -h2, and u = v is -u = -v); it wins only if the minus signs are read as plain algebra
answers.reasoning: Only a concave mirror forms an image of an object at its centre of curvature at the same place: real, inverted and the same size. With the sign convention the object height h1 is positive and the image height is negative, so \(h_1 = -h_2\); object and image are both in front of the mirror, so u and v are both negative, written \(-u = -v\). A convex mirror always forms a smaller, virtual image, so A and C are wrong. Option B says the same equations in another form, so as plain algebra it is not different from D.
Pressure is newton per square metre, which in base units is \(\mathrm{kg/(m\,s^2)}\). Power is joule per second: a joule is \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2/s^2}\), so power is \(\mathrm{kg\,m^2/s^3}\).

1 is true: connecting resistors in parallel lowers the total resistance. 2 is false: it is the inverse of the effective resistance that equals the sum of the inverses, \(\frac{1}{R} = \frac{1}{R_1} + \frac{1}{R_2} + \dots\). 3 is true: every resistor has the same potential difference across it. 4 is false: the current divides, with more current through the smaller resistance.

answers.runnerUp: B (4), if each lens is counted as bending the ray only once instead of at both its surfaces
answers.reasoning: From the figure, the ray changes direction on reflection at the concave mirror (1) and at the plane mirror (2). It then refracts on entering and on leaving the convex lens (3, 4), and on entering and on leaving the lens of the eye (5, 6) before meeting on the retina. So the path changes 6 times.

answers.reasoning: The fluoride in toothpaste makes tooth enamel stronger and so helps it resist decay. Removing dirt and polishing the teeth are done by the mild abrasive powder in the paste, not by the fluoride.

Phosphorous acid \(\mathrm{H_3PO_3}\) has three hydrogen atoms, but one is joined directly to the phosphorus atom and cannot be given away as \(\mathrm{H^+}\). Only the two hydrogens in the OH groups ionise, so its basicity is 2.

answers.value: Covalent bonds, tetrahedral arrangement, three-dimensional structure (1, 3, 4)
answers.reasoning: In diamond every carbon atom is joined by covalent bonds to four other carbon atoms placed at the corners of a tetrahedron, building a rigid three-dimensional network. The hexagonal layered structure belongs to graphite, not diamond.
Polycythemia is a disease in which too many red blood cells are made. Radioactive phosphorus-32 is used to treat it. Cobalt-60 is used for cancer radiotherapy and iodine isotopes for the thyroid.
A glucose molecule is \(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\): 6 carbon atoms and 12 hydrogen atoms, so the ratio is \(6 : 12 = 1 : 2\).

answers.value: Use: radiotherapy; velocity: same as light; ionising power: very low; penetrating power: very high
answers.reasoning: Gamma rays are used in radiotherapy (S); smoke detectors use alpha particles. They are electromagnetic waves, so they travel with the speed of light (T). Compared with alpha and beta, their ionising power is very low (R) and their penetrating power is very high (P).

Statement 3 is true: ceramics are brittle and do not let water through. Statement 2 is true: bone china, made with bone ash, is harder and stronger than ordinary porcelain. answers.reasoning: Slaked lime and chlorine give bleaching powder: \(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2 + Cl_2 \rightarrow CaOCl_2 + H_2O}\). Sodium carbonate and sulphuric acid give \(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4 + H_2CO_3}\), so Q is \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3}\). Bleaching powder with sulphuric acid gives \(\mathrm{CaSO_4 + H_2O + Cl_2}\), so R is \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\).
pH 10 means \(\mathrm{pOH} = 14 - 10 = 4\), so \([\mathrm{OH^-}] = 10^{-4}\) M. NaOH gives one \(\mathrm{OH^-}\) per formula unit, so its molarity is \(10^{-4} = 0.0001\) M.

Here an acidic salt means a salt whose solution in water is acidic: the salt of a strong acid with a weak base, such as ammonium chloride. Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid and phosphoric acid form such salts, while carbonic acid is too weak an acid to do so. So the answer is 1, 3, 4.
answers.notice: The answer depends on what "acidic salt" means. In chemistry an acid salt keeps a replaceable hydrogen (like \(\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\)), which gives (B); the textbook sense used here is a salt whose solution is acidic, which gives MSTA's key (A). answers.value: High melting point and slippery layers
answers.reasoning: Graphite is made of layers that slide easily over each other, which makes it slippery, and its high melting point lets it work as a lubricant even in hot machine parts. The other statements are true of graphite but do not explain its use as a lubricant.
In water the acid ionises, giving \(\mathrm{H^+}\) ions, and adding it to water dilutes it. No base is present, so there is no neutralisation and no salt is formed.

In an acid, blue litmus turns red and methyl red is red. Phenolphthalein stays colourless in an acid, and turmeric stays yellow in an acid (it turns red only in a base).
Chlorine has valency 1, so in \(\mathrm{YCl_3}\) the valency of Y is 3. Oxygen has valency 2, so crossing the valencies gives \(\mathrm{Y_2O_3}\).

answers.value: Hydrogen is the reducing agent and cupric oxide is the oxidising agent (2, 3)
answers.reasoning: Hydrogen takes oxygen from copper oxide and is itself oxidised to water, so hydrogen is the reducing agent. Cupric oxide gives up its oxygen to hydrogen and is reduced to copper, so it is the oxidising agent.
Number of moles \(= \frac{6.022 \times 10^{25}}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} = 100\). One mole of water has mass 18 g, so the mass is \(100 \times 18 = 1800\) g.

In A each side has 2 Na, 2 O and 2 H atoms, and the charges add to zero on both sides. B has 4 \(\mathrm{OH^-}\), which needs 4 O and 4 H on the left; C and D write ions that do not exist, \(\mathrm{OH_2^-}\) and \(\mathrm{Na_2^+}\).
A name ending in '-yne' means a carbon-carbon triple bond. Ethyne and propyne are alkynes; propane has only single bonds and ethene has a double bond.
The zincate ion is \(\mathrm{ZnO_2^{2-}}\), so two sodium ions balance it, giving sodium zincate \(\mathrm{Na_2ZnO_2}\). It forms when zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide.

answers.reasoning: Statement 1: iron combines with oxygen (in moist air) to form reddish brown iron oxide, which is rust, so it is true. Statement 2: a zinc coating (galvanising) keeps air and moisture away from the iron, so it is true as well.

Zinc and aluminium are amphoteric metals: they give hydrogen gas with dilute hydrochloric acid and also with caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) solution, forming sodium zincate and sodium aluminate. Na and K react with water itself, Fe does not react with the alkali, and Cu and Ag do not react with dilute HCl.

The mixture containing nitrogen is producer gas, leaving water gas for row 1 (water gas is really \(\mathrm{CO + H_2}\), so the printed \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) in row 1 is a misprint for CO).

answers.value: Dark red, orange red, green, greenish blue, dark purple
answers.reasoning: Universal indicator is red in strong acid (low pH), turns orange as the acid weakens, green at neutral pH 7, blue as the solution becomes basic and purple in strong base (high pH). So increasing pH runs from dark red to dark purple.
Smoke is solid particles in a gas, an aerosol. Gelatin is listed with sol. Soap froth is gas in a liquid, a foam. Milk is fat droplets in water, an emulsion. That is 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c.
Platinum, palladium and rhodium are noble metals that hardly react at all. Calcium is a very reactive metal, high in the reactivity series, so it is the odd one out.

answers.reasoning: Aluminium phosphide tablets give off phosphine gas, which kills insects in stored grain. Treating food with a gas or smoke like this is fumigation, the method called 'smoking' here. Pasteurisation and freezing use heat and cold, and irradiation uses rays, not a chemical.

Energy flows one way in an ecosystem: from the sun through producers to consumers and is lost as heat. Nutrients are used again and again, returned to the soil by decomposers, so their flow is cyclic.
Root hair cells have a more concentrated sap than the soil water, so water moves into them through the cell membrane by osmosis. Water moving into a cell this way is called endosmosis.
Lizards and snakes are reptiles with a three-chambered heart. The crocodile is the reptile with a four-chambered heart, so it is the odd one out.

answers.value: Early leaf fall and late flowering (P, R)
answers.runnerUp: C, if every listed symptom, including yellowing and a weak stem, is accepted for phosphorus
answers.reasoning: Phosphorus deficiency causes leaves to fall early and delays flowering, along with stunted growth. Yellowing of leaves is the typical sign of nitrogen deficiency, so P and R are the effects of phosphorus deficiency.

The figure labels X with a lignified cell wall, Y with a thin cell wall and Z with a thick cell wall. Lignified walls belong to sclerenchyma, thin walls to parenchyma, and walls thickened at the corners to collenchyma.

To find the pH of soil, a sample of soil is shaken with water, about two parts of water to one part of soil, allowed to settle, and the clear liquid is tested with pH paper or universal indicator. MSTA writes this proportion as 2:1 (water to soil).
answers.notice: The usual method takes 1 part soil to 2 parts water, so (A) 1:2 is also right if the ratio is read as soil to water. MSTA's key gives (C) 2:1. In PYQ Vault mocks this question is awarded to every candidate.

answers.runnerUp: A, if the buds formed at the leaf tips of the walking fern (Adiantum caudatum) are meant
answers.reasoning: Adiantum is a fern, a pteridophyte. Ferns reproduce by spores formed in sporangia on the underside of their leaves.

The nephron is the filtering unit of the kidney and the ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder, so both belong to the excretory system. The uterus and fallopian tube are reproductive organs.
Alpha, beta, delta and PP cells make up the islets of Langerhans, which are in the pancreas. The pancreas lies just behind (below) the stomach.
Plants store some waste products as resins and gums, especially in old xylem (heartwood), which no longer carries water.

In the Venn diagram L is found only in the plant cell, N only in the animal cell, and M in both. Chloroplasts occur only in plant cells, lysosomes are typical of animal cells, and vacuoles occur in both (large in plant cells, small in animal cells).
Thrombocytes, or platelets, help blood to clot at a wound. Leucocytes fight infection, erythrocytes carry oxygen, and osteocytes are bone cells.
Clostridium difficile, Clostridium perfringens and Clostridium botulinum are all bacteria of the genus Clostridium. Cerevisiae is the species name of yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

answers.runnerUp: A, if arsenic in electronic parts (e-waste) is meant
answers.reasoning: Mining and processing of ores leaves waste containing harmful elements such as lead, arsenic and cadmium. Arsenic is therefore listed as a part of mining waste.

answers.value: P-power, Q-by-product, R-end product, S-raw material
answers.reasoning: In the leaf factory, sunlight (P) supplies the power, carbon dioxide and water (S) are the raw materials, glucose (R) is the end product, and oxygen and water (Q) are given out as by-products.
At the tip of a nerve fibre the chemical acetylcholine is released, which carries the impulse across the gap (synapse) to the next cell.
A person with Turner syndrome is female with only one X chromosome, so the chromosomes are 44 autosomes plus a single X, 45 in all.
Equisetum (horsetail) has true roots, stem, leaves and conducting tissue but no seeds, and reproduces by spores, so it belongs to Pteridophyta.
Cholera and hepatitis (types A and E) spread through contaminated food and water. Leprosy, pneumonia, influenza and measles spread by contact or through the air.
Chlamydomonas is a unicellular alga, Aspergillus is a fungus, Volvox is a colonial organism grouped under Protista, and a bacteriophage is a virus that infects bacteria. All four pairs are correct.
In the pyramid of energy, energy falls at every step: phytoplankton to zooplankton to pomfret fish to bear. The bear is at the top level and has the least energy, so it passes on the least.

The carrier father (\(\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}\)) passes either the normal or the sickle gene, while the normal mother (\(\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}\)) passes only the normal gene. So half the children are \(\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^A}\) (normal) and half are \(\mathrm{Hb^A Hb^S}\) (carriers); none suffer.

answers.value: Krebs cycle and electron transport chain (Q, R)
answers.reasoning: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm. The Krebs cycle takes place in the mitochondrial matrix and the electron transport chain on the inner mitochondrial membrane.

answers.runnerUp: A, only if 'tropic movement' is read as something roots do not show (it is the general name for all of them)
answers.reasoning: Roots grow towards gravity (gravitropism) and towards water (hydrotropism), which are tropic movements. Movement towards light is shown by the shoot; roots do not bend towards light (they grow away from it).

Carrying a substance that is made or absorbed in one part of the body to another part is called transportation. Root pressure is only one force in plants, and respiration and excretion are different life processes.

DNA has the bases adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine. Uracil is found in RNA, not DNA, so statement B is false. The double-helix structure, given by Watson and Crick, is the same in all organisms, and each chromosome holds one DNA molecule.

answers.value: K-ovule, L-polar nuclei, M-egg cell, N-pollen tube
answers.reasoning: In the figure, N points to the dark tube that grows down the style and curves into the ovule, so N is the pollen tube. Only option C has this; K points to the ovule, L to the polar nuclei in the middle of the embryo sac and M to the egg cell near the opening where the pollen tube enters.

A tadpole breathes with gills, a whale with lungs and an earthworm through its moist skin. Cockroaches and grasshoppers breathe through tracheae, a shark through gills and a frog mainly through lungs and skin, so the other options are wrong.
Sunscreen lotions use zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, which reflect and absorb the harmful ultraviolet rays of sunlight before they reach the skin.

Nandur Madhyameshwar bird sanctuary in Nashik district attracts large numbers of migratory birds, so it is called the 'Bharatpur of Maharashtra', after the famous bird sanctuary at Bharatpur in Rajasthan.
Covaxin, India's own Covid-19 vaccine, was developed by Bharat Biotech, Hyderabad, with ICMR. Serum Institute made Covishield.

The United States produces the largest total amount of electricity from burning municipal solid waste, from a large number of waste-to-energy plants. Japan burns a larger share of its own waste, but the total output of the United States is greater. MSTA's key gives America.
answers.notice: This depends on how it is measured: Japan burns the largest share of its waste for energy, while the United States produces the most electricity from waste in total. MSTA's key gives (B). In PYQ Vault mocks this question is awarded to every candidate.

When the kidneys fail, a dialysis machine filters the blood outside the body to remove urea and other wastes and then returns it. It does the work of the kidneys artificially; it does not change the blood or replace the kidney.
Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer made the first recombinant DNA in 1973, joining a gene into a bacterial plasmid, and are called the fathers of genetic engineering.
Ebola, influenza, AIDS and SARS are caused by viruses. Anthrax and cholera are caused by bacteria, so any group containing 2 or 3 is wrong.
In India the domestic supply has a potential difference of 220 V between the live and neutral wires, at a frequency of 50 Hz.
A liquid has a definite volume (2), a gas is highly compressible (1), plasma is a super energetic state of matter (4) and a Bose-Einstein condensate has super low density (3).
